tower-of-hanoi.title: Determine descending placement order
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final stack on any peg must be built from the largest disk at the bottom to the smallest at the top; this ordering tells you which disk should be placed next.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to decide which disk to move onto the goal peg next.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If the goal peg must end as [5,4,3,2,1], you must place disk 5 first, then 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks for a larger move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, ensure no smaller disks sit above it on its source peg and that the destination peg does not contain any smaller disks that would be underneath it; relocate those smaller disks to an auxiliary peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the disk you intend to move is not the topmost on its peg, or the destination peg has a smaller top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 5 from peg 0 to peg 2, first move disks 1 and 4 off peg 0 and disks 2 and 3 off peg 2 to another peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use auxiliary peg for temporary storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a disk must be moved but its target peg is occupied, place the disk onto a third peg; the auxiliary peg may already contain a larger disk, which can safely serve as a base for smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to free a peg or hold a smaller disk temporarily.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg 1 holds disk 4 and you need to store disk 2, you can move disk 2 onto peg 1 because 4 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid premature placement on goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a smaller disk onto the final destination peg until all larger disks that must be below it have already been placed there; otherwise the larger disk will have no legal spot.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When considering moving a disk onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not move disk 1 onto peg 2 before disks 5 and 4 have been placed there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Re‑stack displaced smaller disks after larger ones
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After a larger disk has been moved to its final position, move any smaller disks that were temporarily stored back onto the same peg in descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after completing the placement of a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 to peg 2, move disks 4, 3, 2, 1 onto peg 2 in that order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track top disks and legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date view of the topmost disk on each peg and verify that a proposed move respects the rule that only the top disk may move and a larger disk cannot be placed on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before writing or executing each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg 1’s top is disk 3, you cannot move disk 4 onto peg 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate and verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the full move list, replay the moves from the initial state to ensure every move is legal and the final arrangement matches the goal configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have written the complete sequence of moves, before submitting.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run through the moves step‑by‑step; if the final state is not [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, adjust the sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move decomposition
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move n disks from a source peg to a destination peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk, and finally recursively move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary peg onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the problem reduces to moving a contiguous stack of disks that are all on the same peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving three disks from peg 0 to peg 2 uses the pattern: move 2 disks to peg 1, move disk 3 to peg 2, move 2 disks from peg 1 to peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Two‑phase gathering strategy
tower-of-hanoi.principle: First gather all non‑largest disks onto a single auxiliary peg in correct descending order, then move the largest disk directly to the goal peg, and finally transfer the gathered stack onto the goal using the remaining peg as auxiliary.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest disk is not on the goal peg and the smaller disks are scattered across pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Collect disks 1‑4 on peg 1, move disk 5 to peg 2, then move the stack of disks 1‑4 from peg 1 to peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving a particular disk without checking the size of the destination's top disk, forgetting the core rule of the puzzle.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk's size with the top disk of the destination peg; allow the move only if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may generate a move for a disk that is buried under smaller disks, overlooking the rule that only the top disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a representation of each peg's stack and verify that the chosen disk is the current top before issuing a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Temporarily placing a small disk on the goal peg before a larger disk that must be below it
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to clear a source peg by moving a small disk onto the goal peg, not realizing that a larger disk later needs to be placed underneath.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: When the goal peg is the final destination, postpone placing any smaller disks there until all larger required disks have been placed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Leaving blocking disks on the target peg when moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to clear the destination peg of smaller disks before moving a larger one onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving a larger disk to a peg, ensure the peg is empty or its top disk is larger; if not, relocate the smaller disks first.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Failing to verify that the final configuration matches the goal
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop after producing a move list without checking whether the resulting state equals the target arrangement.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move sequence, simulate the entire process from the initial state and compare the final state to the goal; adjust if they differ.
